column1: The transformer architecture relies on self-attention mechanisms to process sequences in parallel, replacing recurrent layers entirely.
Backpropagation computes gradients of the loss function with respect to each weight by applying the chain rule layer by layer.
Convolutional neural networks apply learned filters to detect spatial patterns like edges, textures, and shapes in images.
Gradient descent iteratively updates model parameters in the direction that minimizes the loss function.
Transfer learning reuses a model trained on a large dataset for a different but related task by fine-tuning the final layers.
Recurrent neural networks process sequential data by maintaining a hidden state that captures information from previous timesteps.
Batch normalization normalizes layer inputs to reduce internal covariate shift and accelerate training convergence.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to prevent overfitting and improve generalization.
Attention mechanisms allow neural networks to focus on the most relevant parts of the input when producing each output element.
Generative adversarial networks consist of a generator and discriminator trained in opposition to produce realistic synthetic data.
